findings.title: Table readers do not establish declared row/decoded-byte bounds before allocation, and scores/Parquet can successfully exceed them.
findings.evidence: Scores cap rows1/decoded64 returned2rows/476bytes and finish succeeded. Repeated1000-row int64 Parquet had row-group total_byte_size97, passed decoded cap512, returned DataFrame8132bytes and finish succeeded. CSV maxrows1 allocated a2-row/148byte DataFrame before rejecting.
findings.effect: Successful completion can falsely imply resource-bounded transport, and oversized external table inputs can allocate before rejection. Parquet encoded-uncompressed bytes are not a decoded DataFrame upper bound.
findings.recommendation: Bound CSV/scores via streaming preflight before pandas allocation; enforce rows/decoded limits on scores too. Constrain registered Parquet encoding/schema and use a conservative decoded leaf/row/variable-width bound before pandas read, then verify measured memory. Preserve all precision-safe score fields and tuples.

findings.title: Payload and receipt are published before decoded validity/equivalence is checked.
findings.evidence: CSV maxrows1 and NPY decoded cap8 both raised on __call__, yet payload_published:true and receipt_published:true. Reopening the same sink then failed at the same reader limit; completion could not succeed.
findings.effect: Invalid or out-of-budget staged output becomes an append-only committed artifact and poisons same-claim resume. The write exception does not leave only retained staging.
findings.recommendation: Perform bounded decode and exact equivalence on staging before promotion; preflight the complete receipt/evidence quota too. Publish only a verified artifact/receipt transaction and preserve failed staging. Do not repair by overwriting/deleting committed evidence.

findings.title: Temporary reservation uses logical capacity while usage charges allocated filesystem blocks.
findings.evidence: max_artifact_bytes=max_temporary_bytes=1024 reserved successfully; a136-byte NPY used4096 allocated bytes. _guard rejected only after retained staging usage4096 exceeded the1024 temporary cap.
findings.effect: The stated hard temporary boundary can be exceeded by the failed write it is supposed to bound. _usage additionally excludes directory allocation, so directory overhead needs an explicit accounted contract.
findings.recommendation: Reserve using allocation-unit rounding and all declared staging/evidence overhead before write, with a documented treatment for directories/metadata. Keep failed staging charged and retained; do not silently delete it to recover quota.

findings.title: Declared artifact names can collide after JSON bundle suffix mapping or conflict as file/directory prefixes.
findings.evidence: Inventory {a.json:json,a.json.bundle:array} was claimed; both map to the same artifact path. First JSON committed, second write failed as unreceipted payload, finish/reenter both failed as uncommitted publication.
findings.effect: An accepted static inventory can be impossible to complete and permanently non-resumable after a valid first publication.
findings.recommendation: Before namespace claim, require injective mapped paths and reject overlapping file/directory or JSON-bundle-contained paths. Keep normal D60/H37 inventories valid.

findings.title: Exact-match fast path bypasses timing-value validation.
findings.evidence: Known conditional_bootstrap.json with preparation_seconds:-1 and bootstrap_seconds:true was accepted on first write because ordered JSON matched. A subsequent changed-timing resume rejected invalid engineering timing.
findings.effect: Validity depends on whether timings changed, even though the exception is intended only for valid engineering durations.
findings.recommendation: Validate the exact known top-level timing fields on both saved and expected values before exact-equality or timing-tolerant returns. Nested timing/scientific fields remain exact.
findings.closed_observation: The formerly overbroad normal_bootstrap_ filename matcher is already fixed in8fca5; the unknown-filename changed timing probe correctly rejects.

strengths: Identity-bound output namespace, root-relative private empty cache lock and no-replace publication provide a solid append-only base.
Physical file usage includes max(logical bytes,allocated blocks); failed staging remains visible and charged rather than deleted.
NPY header version/object/order/byte-length checks precede np.load in the reader.
JSON uses accepted exact multiplicity bundle/code/context binding; ordinary non-timing JSON fields and order are compared exactly.
On tested source8fca5, timing tolerance names are exact; unknown filenames and changed scientific values reject.
The10 original selected transport tests pass in3.11s, including corruption, existing resume, symlink/refused dual writer and capped numpy file-descriptor bypass.
